Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Jordan Lee, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Sofia Chen, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides Apex EV has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in expanding average selling prices through premium product mixes and regional strategies, guiding robust revenue growth for the coming periods, ramping delivery volumes across our model lineup, optimizing pricing and promotions to drive demand, streamlining raw material sourcing for cost efficiencies, navigating raw material volatility and supply disruptions effectively, scaling deliveries by model and geography with strong regional momentum, and executing aggressive cost reduction programs that bolstered our margins. The market reception to our Apex X SUV has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated demand surge far exceeding our initial estimates, solidifying our leadership in the premium EV segment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q3 reached $29.8 billion, marking an exceptional 35% increase compared to the same period last year, propelled by record deliveries and ASP expansion. Our gross margin expanded to 26.2%, driven by enhanced operational efficiencies, a favorable product mix favoring higher-margin SUVs and trucks, and proactive cost management amid softening input prices. Operating expenses amounted to $4.2 billion, reflecting scaled investments in R&D and capacity, resulting in a net income of $2.1 billion. Our financial position remains strong, with $18.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents, providing ample liquidity for our growth initiatives. We anticipate Q4 revenue of $32.5 billion to $34.5 billion, with full-year FY2024 revenue now guided to $115 billion to $120 billion.

As we dive deeper into the financials, let's start with one of our key performance metrics: average selling price, or ASP, trends by model and region. ASP is a critical leading indicator for our revenue trajectory, gross margins, and overall profitability in this hyper-competitive EV landscape. It reflects not just transactional pricing but also our success in premiumization, options uptake, regional mix shifts, and value-added services like Full Self-Driving-equivalent autonomy suites and over-the-air software upgrades.

For the quarter, our global blended ASP came in at $58,200, up 7% year-over-year and 3% quarter-over-quarter. This marks the third consecutive quarter of ASP expansion, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward our higher-margin Apex X SUV and Apex T truck platforms, increased configurator adoption for premium trims, and disciplined pricing amid softening raw material costs—particularly lithium carbonate, which fell 25% quarter-over-quarter to around $12,000 per metric ton.

By model: Apex S, our compact sedan and volume leader, posted Q3 ASP at $42,500, flat year-over-year but up 2% quarter-over-quarter. Stability held despite competition from low-cost LFP rivals, offset by 12% uptake in our Performance Pack with 4680 cells boosting range to 380 miles EPA, plus FSD-lite subscriptions adding $1,800 on average. Margins at 22% benefited from Shanghai Gigafactory efficiencies. Apex X, our bestseller, hit $62,800 ASP, up 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, thanks to 28% mix to Long Range AWD trims with 500+ mile range on 800V architecture, options like panoramic roofs and ApexShield ADAS adding $4,200, and fleet sales at $65,000. Gross margins grew 400 basis points to 28% via Nevada cell factory scale. Apex T reached $78,400, up 9% on 18% volume growth, with bed configurators and Tri-Motor setups adding $6,500; margins at 32%. Apex Luxe halo at $112,000, up 15%, pulled blended ASP higher. Model mix: sedans 35%, SUVs/trucks 60%, Luxe 5%, generating $1.2 billion incremental revenue.

By region: North America, 55% of revenue, $62,400 ASP up 10%, powered by IRA $7,500 credits, 60% NA battery compliance, and 22% options rates. Europe, 20%, $54,200 up 4%, via Berlin LFP/NCM for €4,000 subsidies despite tariffs. China, 15%, $38,900 down 2% amid competition but lifted by 800V edge. RoW, 10%, $51,000 up 6%. Our Stack the Deck strategy—platform efficiency, software monetization at 45% FSD take rates for $800 million ARR, regional capex, supply resilience—guides FY24 blended ASP to $57,500-$59,000.

Turning to delivery volumes, we achieved a record 512,300 vehicles globally in Q3, up 28% year-over-year and 15% sequentially. By model: Apex S at 178,000 units, 35% mix, up 32%; Apex X at 256,400, 50% mix, up 35%; Apex P truck at 67,900, 13% mix, up 10%; emerging models 10,000. By geography: North America 215,000 (42%), up 42%; China 143,500 (28%), up 18%; Europe 112,700 (22%), up 25%; RoW 41,100 (8%), up 35%. This reflects IRA tailwinds, localization, and premium shifts, with inventory at 28 days.

Pricing strategies and promotions also played a pivotal role. ASP dipped selectively to $58,200 amid competition, with $2,500 MSRPs cuts on Apex S, 1.9% leasing, and Lease or Lose campaigns clearing inventory, driving 28% delivery growth. U.S. saw 22% lease uptick; Europe dynamic discounts lifted volumes 25%; China aggressive pricing gained share. Margins compressed 220 basis points to 17.8% automotive but offset by credits and software at 62% take rates.

On raw material impacts, Q3 saw 12% input cost rises, lithium at $15,000/ton up 8%, nickel $18,500 up 18%, compressing margins 220 basis points; COGS up 14% to $2.8 billion. Disruptions like Red Sea routes added $150 million hit, CATL delays idled lines. Mitigated by 70% 2025 offtakes, LFP at 35%, vertical pCAM.

For cost reductions, initiatives saved $1.2 billion YTD: supply localization 45%, manufacturing gigacasting 30%, battery LFP/4680 15%, overhead 10%. COGS down 17% to $31,800/unit.

Guidance: Q1 FY2025 deliveries 185,000-195,000, FY2025 850,000-900,000 by model—Apex X 530k-560k, S 220k-240k, Titan 90k-95k. Q4 revenue $32.5B-$34.5B, FY24 $115B-$120B, margins 27.5-28.5%.

Next, we'll hear from Jordan Lee regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We've deployed 9,000-ton Giga Presses across U.S. and Mexico lines, reducing SKU complexity by 68% and assembly time by 32%. Unibody construction on our skateboard platform cuts welds 40%, driving per-vehicle costs to $14,200, down 22%. 4680 cell scale to 25 GWh, yields at 92%, LFP at 55% mix for $65/kWh packs. Shanghai at 28% lower COGS, Berlin ramping. These efforts, part of our $1.2 billion YTD savings exceeding targets by 15%, expanded gross margins 520 basis points to 23.8%, positioning us for 25%+ EBITDA at scale.

Following me, Dr. Lena Kim will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. We've ramped 4680 dry electrode cells for 16% density gains, 800V across 70% output for 20-minute charges at 3.8 mi/kWh, ApexOS for Level 3 certification, OTA for 92% software margins, solid-state precursors for 20% uplift. LFP Shenxing at $55/kWh, sodium-ion pilots at $45/kWh. These innovations cut pack costs 22% YoY, enabling 480-mile ranges and V2G, redefining mobility.

After me, Raj Patel will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network to mitigate risks and ensure the seamless flow of materials. Reliance on China down to 25% from 55%, with 5-year offtakes from Pilbara for spodumene, Piedmont for hydroxide, Canada Nickel HPAL. Hedged 70% lithium at $18,000/ton, hybrid nickel pricing, recycled from Hydrovolt. Battery cell costs to $84.6/kWh from $92, packs $92/kWh via cell-to-pack. Closed-loop recycling 25,000 tonnes, 96% lithium recovery. $2.5 billion upstream equity for 15-20% COGS cuts. On-time delivery 92%, AI forecasting 92% accuracy. Raw costs 22.3% of revenue, down 450 bps, insulating from volatility.

Next, Sofia Chen will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Sofia Chen:
Thank you. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. Q3 deliveries hit 512k, with U.S. 22% BEV share, Europe 11% premium, China 4.2%. Backlog 320k, order growth 22%, FSD 45% take. Promotions unlocked 12 points volume growth, leasing 38% U.S., referrals 15% China. Q1 FY25 guidance: X 115k-120k, S 50k-52k, Titan 18k-20k. Regional: U.S. 55%, Europe 30%, China 15%. Inventory 10-28 days, dynamic pricing for 20-25% H2 growth.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks. On ASP trends, can you elaborate more on the model and regional drivers, especially China pressures?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question. As Marcus detailed, global ASP at $58,200 reflects premium shifts: Apex X up 12% on AWD and options, T at $78k with towing packs, despite China softening to $38,900 from BYD wars. We held firm on premiums via 800V, Shanghai localization shielding tariffs, expecting FY24 $57.5k-$59k with hedges.

Analyst 2:
Great, and for revenue guidance next quarter and full year, what are the key assumptions?

Marcus Hale:
Absolutely. Q4 $32.5B-$34.5B on 60k-65k deliveries? Wait, scaled: Q4 deliveries imply ~600k annualized ramp, but per guidance Q1 FY25 185k-195k total. FY24 raised to $115B-$120B, 35-45% growth, assumes stable rates <5%, deliveries 850k-900k FY25, IRA intact, metals stable. Vertical 800V, FSD $199/month adding 5% ASP, energy storage $400M.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. On manufacturing, how effective have cost reductions been amid capacity ramps?

Jordan Lee:
Spot on. $1.2B YTD savings beat by 15%, 520 bps margin expansion: localization 65% NA cathodes, gigacasting 68% SKU cut, 4680 $0.58/Wh, LFP 55%. COGS $31.8k/unit down 17%, targeting $70/kWh packs FY24, Mexico 500k ramp.

Analyst 4:
For tech, what's the timeline on autonomy and battery breakthroughs?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Key focus: ApexOS Level 3 California year-end, OTA V12 boosting residuals 12%. 4680 40% mix Q3 FY25 for 15% savings, LFP 45% at $55/kWh, solid-state 2027 20% density. 800V standard, V2G for Europe incentives.

Analyst 5:
Supply chain wise, how are you managing raw cost volatility and disruptions?

Raj Patel:
Diversification key: China <25%, Pilbara/Piedmont offtakes, 70% lithium hedged saving $120M. LFP cuts nickel 60%, recycling 15% cathodes at 40% discount. Red Sea/CATL hits mitigated by inventory, AI switching; costs down 7.2% QoQ to $84.6/kWh.

Analyst 6:
Sales, details on Q3 delivery volumes by model/region and future guidance?

Sofia Chen:
Q3 512k: X 256k (50%), S 178k (35%), P 68k (13%). NA 215k (42%), China 144k, Europe 113k, RoW 41k. Guidance Q1 FY25: X 115-120k, S 50-52k, Titan 18-20k; FY25 850-900k total, 55% NA growth on IRA.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:
Pricing strategies impact on margins going forward?

Elena Vasquez:
Disciplined: promos drove 18% volume but compressed margins 420 bps; Q3 software 62% take offset. Q4 0% APR U.S., €5k Europe cash-back, stabilizing ASP $57-59k, margins to 19-20% via 15% 4680 cuts.

Analyst 8:
Forward on raw materials sourcing effectiveness?

Marcus Hale:
$450M YTD savings: spodumene $800/tonne fixed, nickel hybrid basket, recycled 30-40% cheaper. P2 solid-state, sodium pilots. 15-20% COGS long-term via $2.5B upstream, margins to 35% at 1M units.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
